reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract, a byte-identical Submission with no Submission.* declarations, and the README. The DAG contains only root, so the 12 bare child names are unreserved. All 12 conjuncts are `def … : Prop` in namespace GMT.Ch06. In a scratch build of the frozen project, every child statement elaborates in the comparator's child scope, `exact Submission.<name>` resolves for all 12 children, and the 12-way assembly typechecks against `type_of% GMT.Ch06.main_theorem`. FedererFlemingCompactness follows from its three declared siblings and the parent from the other 11 children, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The contract's `IsLipschitzPushforward` supplies only an `IsRectifiableTriple` representation (θ′ > 0 real, integrable on compacts), confirming the v2 defect. The repaired deformation A3 uses only that. Its σ-finiteness step is kernel-checked as `v3_sigmaFinite_restrict` (via Mathlib `Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable`, `mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`, `ae_restrict_mem₀`), and its tangent-space step as `v3_weightedTangent_congr`, against the actual SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt`/`blowUpMap` definitions (via `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`, `ae_restrict_iff'₀`; μHE[d] is a scalar multiple of μH[d]), both with standard axioms only. Mathlib provides Radon–Nikodym-type uniqueness (`ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite`, `Integrable.ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq`). SimonGMT provides `nVectorPushforward_simple`, `covectorEuclideanNorm` and `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`. Simon Ch. 1 gives 1.12 (μ⌞Y is Borel regular for measurable Y of finite measure), 1.15(2) (inner regularity) and 2.6 (H^m is Borel regular), as cited. There is no Mathlib match for co-area or for Besicovitch–Federer/purely unrectifiable; these are cited from Simon Ch. 3, as SimonGMT omits them. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, 6.1 (Isoperimetric Theorem) and its printed proof (pp. 168–169). Book n = m + 2 ≥ 2: T ∈ D_{n−1}(ℝ^{n+ℓ}) = D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+2+ℓ}), ℓ ≥ 1. The printed proof: apply the scaled deformation theorem 5.3 to T at a scale ρ; S = 0 because ∂T = 0; the polyhedral part P has mass N(ρ)ρ^{n−1} with N(ρ) ∈ ℕ and M(P) ≤ cM(T), so P = 0 for ρ = (2cM(T))^{1/(n−1)}; then T = ∂R with M(R) ≤ cρM(T). It is copied below with the details filled in. Errata applied: “F ∈ F_{n−1}(ρ)” means F ∈ 𝓛_{n−1}(ρ), “since M ≤ cM(T)” means M(P) ≤ cM(T), and the printed last display M(R) ≤ cρM(T) = c′M(T)^{1/(n−1)} should read c′M(T)^{n/(n−1)} (which is equivalent to the claimed M(R)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ cM(T)).

Sibling result used: `DeformationTheorem` (5.3), applied with (m, ℓ+1): currents of degree m+1 in ℝ^{(m+1)+(ℓ+1)}; note (m+1)+(ℓ+1) = m+2+ℓ, so the ambient spaces coincide (in Lean: rewrite `Eucl (m + 1 + (ℓ + 1))` to `Eucl (m + 2 + ℓ)` by the equation m+1+(ℓ+1) = m+2+ℓ; this rewrite has been checked to typecheck).

Proof. Fix m, ℓ ≥ 1, write k := m + 1 = n − 1 ≥ 1 (degree of T), d := m + 2 + ℓ. Let C₀ = C₀(m, ℓ+1) be the constant of `DeformationTheorem` for (m, ℓ+1). Define c := (C₀(2C₀)^{1/k})^{k/(k+1)} (a constant depending only on m, ℓ; take c := 0 if C₀ = 0). Let T ∈ D_k(ℝ^d) be integer multiplicity with compact support and ∂T = 0.

1. (Finite mass.) T = τ(M,θ,ξ) with θ integrable on M ∩ K for compact K. Let χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the compact spt T, K := spt χ. For a test form ω with ‖ω‖ ≤ 1, (1 − χ)ω vanishes near spt T, so T((1−χ)ω) = 0 (a test form supported in the open zero region is annihilated: cover its compact support by finitely many open sets on which T vanishes and use a partition of unity). Hence T(ω) = ∫_M θχ⟨ω, ξ⟩dH^k ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^k, using |⟨ω,ξ⟩| ≤ |ω||ξ| and |ξ| = 1 H^k-a.e. on M (ξ = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame; Cauchy–Binet). So M(T) < ∞, and M(∂T) = M(0) = 0.

2. (Trivial case.) If M(T) = 0 then |T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖ = 0 for all ω, so T = 0; take R := 0 (integer multiplicity with M = ∅, spt R = ∅ compact, ∂R = 0 = T, M(R)^{k/(k+1)} = 0 ≤ c·0). Assume from now on 0 < M(T) < ∞.

3. (Deformation.) Put ρ := (2C₀M(T))^{1/k} if C₀ > 0 (if C₀ = 0, take ρ := 1). By `DeformationTheorem` (with m, ℓ+1, after the dimension rewrite) there are β, Pc = Σ_F β_F[[F]] (F ∈ 𝓛_k(ρ), `IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc`), R ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^d), S ∈ D_k(ℝ^d) with T − Pc = ∂R + S, M(Pc) ≤ C₀M(T), M(R) ≤ C₀ρM(T), M(S) ≤ C₀ρM(∂T) = 0, spt Pc ∪ spt R ⊆ {dist(·, spt T) < 2√d·ρ}; and since T is integer multiplicity, all β_F ∈ ℤ and Pc, R are integer multiplicity.

4. (S = 0.) M(S) = 0, so S = 0 (Step 2's argument).

5. (Pc = 0; printed (1) “M(P) = N(ρ)ρ^{n−1}”.) Claim: if some β_{F₀} ≠ 0 then M(Pc) ≥ |β_{F₀}|ρ^k. Let F₀ = ρ(z + F_α) and K₀ a compact subset of the relative interior F̊₀. Take ω := s·φ·dx^α with s := sign(β_{F₀}), φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d), 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on K₀, and spt φ disjoint from every face F ≠ F₀ with the same direction α (possible: such faces are closed and at positive distance from the compact K₀ ⊆ F̊₀ — those in the same affine k-plane meet F₀ only in its relative boundary, those in parallel planes are at distance ≥ ρ — and only finitely many of them meet a bounded neighbourhood of K₀). Then |ω| ≤ 1 (|dx^α| = 1), and for faces F with direction α′ ≠ α, [[F]](ω) = ∫_F sφ dx^α(e_{α′}) dH^k = 0 (dx^α(e_{α′}) = 0). Hence Pc(ω) = Σ_F β_F[[F]](ω) = |β_{F₀}|∫_{F₀}φ dH^k ≥ |β_{F₀}|H^k(K₀) (φ = 1 on K₀, φ ≥ 0), and Pc(ω) ≤ M(Pc) since ω is mass-admissible. Letting K₀ ↑ F̊₀ gives M(Pc) ≥ |β_{F₀}|H^k(F₀) = |β_{F₀}|ρ^k. If C₀ > 0, M(Pc) ≤ C₀M(T) = ρ^k/2 < ρ^k, so no β_F ∈ ℤ∖{0} occurs; if C₀ = 0, M(Pc) = 0 and again all β_F = 0. Thus Pc = 0.

6. (Conclusion.) From Steps 3–5, T = ∂R (as functionals on test forms, hence `R.boundary = T` by extensionality). R is integer multiplicity. spt R ⊆ {dist(·, spt T) < 2√d ρ} is bounded (spt T compact) and closed (spt R = ℝ^d ∖ zeroRegion, zeroRegion open), hence compact. Finally M(R) ≤ C₀ρM(T) = C₀(2C₀)^{1/k}M(T)^{(k+1)/k}, so M(R)^{k/(k+1)} ≤ (C₀(2C₀)^{1/k})^{k/(k+1)}M(T) = cM(T) (rpow in [0,∞] is monotone; exponent k/(k+1) = (m+1)/(m+2) > 0). If C₀ = 0 then M(R) = 0 and the inequality is trivial. This proves `IsoperimetricTheorem`.
key_steps: T has finite mass (integer multiplicity, compact support); T = 0 is trivial.
Apply the sibling deformation theorem with (m, ℓ+1) after rewriting m+1+(ℓ+1) = m+2+ℓ, at scale ρ = (2C₀M(T))^{1/(m+1)}.
A nonzero integer lattice chain has mass ≥ ρ^{m+1} (test forms ±φdx^α near one face), while M(Pc) ≤ ρ^{m+1}/2; so Pc = 0.
Hence T = ∂R with R integer multiplicity, spt R closed and within 2√d ρ of spt T (compact).
M(R) ≤ C₀ρM(T) = C₀(2C₀)^{1/(m+1)}M(T)^{(m+2)/(m+1)} gives the isoperimetric inequality.
